title: Remove Nodes with Greater Right
description:
You are given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list. Remove every node that has another node with a **strictly greater** value anywhere to its right in the list.

Return the head of the modified linked list. Note that the remaining node values will form a non-increasing sequence. Solve this in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^4].
hints: Scanning right-to-left lets you maintain a single running maximum `maxSoFar` and discard any node with `val < maxSoFar`.
To scan right-to-left in O(1) extra space, reverse the list, filter out nodes smaller than the running maximum, and reverse the filtered list back.

examples.explanation: Nodes 5, 2, and 3 all have 13 or 8 to their right and are removed, leaving [13, 8].
All values are equal (1), so no node has a strictly greater value to its right: [1, 1, 1, 1].
The list is strictly increasing, so only the rightmost node [5] survives.
